issues.legal_issue: A lease provision requiring payment for a lessee-built structure and arbitration of its market value does not postpone the lessor’s right to possession after the lease expires unless the lease makes possession conditional on valuation or payment.
material_facts: The fixed-term lease had expired, and the lessors applied for eviction in rent-control proceedings.
The lease provided that the structure built by the lessees would become the lessors’ property on expiry and that the lessors could then exercise ownership rights.

The lease required the lessors to pay the lessees a share of the structure’s market value; disagreements about value were to be arbitrated, and the lessees had a first charge on sale proceeds if payment was not made within the specified time.
The lease did not expressly provide that the lessees could retain possession until the market value was determined or paid.
The lessees sought a stay of the eviction proceedings while the market value was determined by arbitration.
issues.conclusion: The lease did not give the lessees a right to retain possession after expiry pending valuation or payment. The valuation liability was separable from the lessors’ right to possession, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 108(q) of the Transfer of Property Act, absent a contract or local usage to the contrary, a lessee must put the lessor into possession when the lease ends. The lessee bears the burden of establishing a contrary agreement, which must be indicated by the lease where it concerns the valuable right to possession. The lease’s payment obligation and arbitration mechanism did not create such an agreement; the Rent Controller’s statutory eviction function under section 13 of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act was not concerned with determining market value. The Court distinguished Ethirajulu Naidu v. Ranganathan Chetty, where the lease expressly made surrender of possession conditional on payment for the structure. Section 34 of the Arbitration Act did not warrant staying the eviction proceedings on the facts presented.

rule.if: rent_eviction_proceeding and lease_expired and ownership_vests_at_expiry and compensation_payable and valuation_arbitrable and no_possession_condition and tenant_seeks_arbitration_stay

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought eviction through statutory rent-control proceedings after a tenancy ended.
predicates.ownership_vests_at_expiry: The lease terms made the lessee-built structure the landlord’s property and made ownership rights exercisable when the lease ended.
predicates.compensation_payable: The lease required the landlord to pay the lessee compensation for the structure.
predicates.valuation_arbitrable: The lease provided for arbitration if the parties disagreed about the structure’s market value.
predicates.no_possession_condition: The lease did not expressly make the lessee’s surrender of possession conditional on valuation or payment.
predicates.tenant_seeks_arbitration_stay: The lessee asked to pause eviction proceedings while arbitrators determined the structure’s value.
predicates.lessor_may_take_possession_on_lease_expi: The landlord may obtain possession when the lease ends without waiting for valuation or payment.

issues.definition: When a lease ends and gives the landlord ownership at expiry, a compensation obligation and arbitration over value do not prevent possession at expiry if the lease does not make surrender conditional on valuation or payment.
